hooks.text: Swapping our Sun with Betelgeuse swallows Jupiter's orbit.
A star in Orion would swallow Jupiter inside our solar system.
Replacing our Sun with one star swallows the orbit of Jupiter.

title: The Star Big Enough to SWALLOW Jupiter
description: Betelgeuse is so immense that swapping it with our Sun would engulf Jupiter. In 2019, this colossal red supergiant shocked astronomers by blowing off part of its own surface.

beats.text: Swapping our Sun with Betelgeuse swallows Jupiter's orbit.
beats.visual: Diagram comparing Betelgeuse's radius to planetary orbits of the Solar System
queries: Betelgeuse orbit of Jupiter comparison diagram

beats.text: Its edge would engulf Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
beats.visual: Artist concept comparing Betelgeuse to inner planets of the Solar System

beats.text: Yet Betelgeuse is only about ten million years old.
beats.visual: Wide-field night sky photograph of constellation Orion featuring Betelgeuse

beats.text: The star lost most of its visible brightness in late 2019.
beats.visual: ESO Very Large Telescope SPHERE comparison of Betelgeuse before and during dimming, 2019

beats.text: Hubble showed it had blown off a huge piece of its surface.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope ultraviolet image of Betelgeuse disk showing surface ejection, 2020
queries: Hubble Betelgeuse surface mass ejection image

beats.text: That ejected gas cooled into a massive dust cloud.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Betelgeuse ejecting a colossal plume of surface material, 2020
queries: Betelgeuse surface mass ejection NASA illustration
Betelgeuse dust cloud artist concept ESO

beats.text: Astronomers think it will explode as a supernova within 100,000 years.
beats.visual: ALMA submillimeter radio portrait of Betelgeuse's atmosphere

beats.text: That blast will be bright enough to see in broad daylight.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a bright supernova visible in daytime sky from Earth

beats.text: Until then, few stars match the sheer scale of this titan.
beats.visual: Herschel Space Observatory far-infrared view of Betelgeuse bow shock
queries: Betelgeuse bow shock Herschel Space Observatory
